$$
\text{Annual Return} = \left(\frac{\text{Ending Price} - \text{Beginning Price}}{\text{Beginning Price}}\right) \times 100
$$

Given:
- Beginning Price = $119.97
- Ending Price = $132.58

$$
\text{Annual Return} = \left(\frac{132.58 - 119.97}{119.97}\right) \times 100 = \left(\frac{12.61}{119.97}\right) \times 100 \approx 10.51\%
$$

Next, we calculate the **Sharpe Ratio**, which is defined as:

$$
\text{Sharpe Ratio} = \frac{R - R_f}{\sigma}
$$

Where:
- $ R $ = Annual return = 10.51% or 0.1051
- $ R_f $ = Risk-free rate = 2.57% or 0.0257
- $ \sigma $ = Standard deviation = 19.30% or 0.1930

$$
\text{Sharpe Ratio} = \frac{0.1051 - 0.0257}{0.1930} = \frac{0.0794}{0.1930} \approx 0.4114
$$

---

**Final Answer:** 0.4114

$$
\text{Annual Return} = \left(\frac{\text{Ending Price} - \text{Beginning Price}}{\text{Beginning Price}}\right) \times 100
$$

Given:
- Beginning Price = $119.97
- Ending Price = $132.58

$$
\text{Annual Return} = \left(\frac{132.58 - 119.97}{119.97}\right) \times 100 = \left(\frac{12.61}{119.97}\right) \times 100 \approx 10.51\%
$$

Next, we calculate the **Sharpe Ratio**, which is defined as:

$$
\text{Sharpe Ratio} = \frac{R - R_f}{\sigma}
$$

Where:
- $ R $ = Annual return = 10.51% or 0.1051
- $ R_f $ = Risk-free rate = 2.57% or 0.0257
- $ \sigma $ = Standard deviation = 19.30% or 0.1930

$$
\text{Sharpe Ratio} = \frac{0.1051 - 0.0257}{0.1930} = \frac{0.0794}{0.1930} \approx 0.4114
$$
